title: PINN Design Stack & Feedback Loops
description: A ten-stage design architecture showing how upstream scientific choices constrain downstream realization and how validation evidence drives targeted redesign.
represents: The stack organizes a PINN study as four coupled phases rather than as neural-network training alone. It begins with the physical problem and computational role, translates these into representation and physics-enforcement choices, realizes them numerically, and closes the loop through reliability-oriented evaluation.
interpretation: The vertical path is a typical design sequence, not a universal recipe. Bidirectional phase links indicate strong interdependence, while evaluation feedback should return the workflow to the earliest plausible design cause. A redesign is accepted only after numerical, physical, robustness, uncertainty, and computational-cost checks improve.

phases.title: Problem Framing
phases.summary: Defines the scientific system, numerical demands, intended PINN role, and representation interface.

phases.title: PINN Formulation
phases.summary: Defines the trainable approximation and how governing knowledge and differential operators are realized.

phases.title: PINN Training
phases.summary: Defines where objectives are enforced, how losses are balanced, and how optimization is performed.

phases.title: PINN Reliability
phases.summary: Determines whether the resulting model is numerically accurate, physically faithful, robust, efficient, and reusable.

stages.title: Physical Problem Definition
stages.subtitle: Defines the physical system and its numerical demands
stages.summary: The governing structure, geometry, conditions, scales, regularity, and available data determine every downstream design choice.

stages.title: Computational Role
stages.subtitle: Defines the intended use of the PINN
stages.summary: A PINN intended for forward solution, inverse recovery, discovery, control, or repeated queries requires different outputs, training data, and validation criteria.

stages.title: Inputs and Outputs
stages.subtitle: Defines the representation interface
stages.summary: Input and output choices define the model interface, dimensionality, state coverage, latent variables, and quantities available for physics enforcement.

stages.title: Representation / Architecture
stages.subtitle: Defines the trainable approximation model
stages.summary: The ansatz and basis determine approximation capacity, inductive bias, spectral behavior, derivative regularity, and optimization geometry.

stages.title: Physics Enforcement
stages.subtitle: Defines how governing knowledge constrains the model
stages.summary: Physics may enter through strong, weak, integral, hard, conservative, interface, or constitutive mechanisms with different admissibility and cost consequences.

stages.title: Differentiation and Residual Evaluation
stages.subtitle: Defines how operators and derivatives are computed
stages.summary: Derivative order and operator realization control residual fidelity, gradient quality, memory, solver calls, and numerical stability.

stages.title: Sampling / Collocation
stages.subtitle: Defines where the loss is enforced
stages.summary: Collocation determines domain and constraint coverage and therefore which residual information enters the gradient.

stages.title: Loss Construction and Balancing
stages.subtitle: Defines the optimization objective
stages.summary: The composite objective couples data and physics; its scaling and competition determine signal quality, constraint balance, and convergence.

stages.title: Optimization and Training Strategy
stages.subtitle: Defines how the objective is minimized
stages.summary: Optimizer sequence, learning rate, initialization, curricula, transfer, and stopping determine convergence speed and stability.

stages.title: Evaluation and Validation
stages.subtitle: Determines reliability and guides redesign
stages.summary: Validation must combine solution error, residual diagnostics, physical fidelity, robustness, uncertainty, inverse recovery, computational cost, and benchmarks.
